Ayesha Hoca is engaging, and she tells the topics nicely. I can tell that she is knowledgeable. However, the major issue was that she was too disorganized throughout the semester. First of all, it is unacceptable to change the syllabus in the middle of the semester because the syllabus is given to us to prepare for upcoming classes, assignments, exams, etc. She made that extremely hard. Secondly, throughout the semester, we only covered 7 chapters. I don't know how the whole semester has gone with this amount of topics, and we literally talked about the differences between a psychiatrist and a psychologist for weeks. Thirdly, we were supposed to have in-class assignments, and our attendance was supposed to matter for a grade, but it turned out that it didn't matter, and we were given a pretty easy take-home assignment substituting for the in-class. Fourth, there are times when Ayesha Hoca came to class late and notifying about it 10 minutes before the class. This is extremely disrespectful and infuriating behavior because I don't live on campus, and I came a long way from home. I came on time, but the instructor didn't. I wanted to be understanding and excuse her because this is her first year, but I know that there are other instructors who started teaching this year and didn't behave like this. So, it felt unfair not to tell these problems. Therefore, unfortunately, this class was a disappointment, and it felt disorganized.

I know it must have been tough for her to teach almost every clinical psychology course this semester right after moving to a new country and adjusting to everything, but unfortunately, this course was a real disappointment. We couldn't finish the syllabus, the online portion was really ineffective (which wasn’t her fault), and the exams were graded quite harshly. Nothing I wrote in the exam was wrong—she even told me that—but I lost 5 points from LETTER grade simply because I didn’t link my ideas better. This isn’t an ENG 101/2 class, so my analytic thinking, the relevance of my ideas, and overall understanding should have been the focus. She later created a bonus assignment to compensate for that, but it was still a tough period for many of us, and it drained our motivation. I really hope things improve moving forward. I know she’s passionate about her work and seems to be a great therapist, so with the right structure and approach, her courses could definitely improve, and I think she will take all this constructive criticism and work towards her future courses.

course: I believe what truly sets this course apart is its strong emphasis on practical application, which goes beyond simply learning theory. Throughout the course, we not only studied various clinical interview techniques in depth but also had numerous opportunities to actively practice and refine these skills in simulated therapy sessions. This hands-on approach allowed us to gain confidence and a deeper understanding of how to effectively use these techniques in real-life clinical settings. The course content is thoughtfully structured and carefully prepared, striking a great balance between theory and practice. As a result, it creates an engaging and enjoyable learning experience that is both highly educational and relevant especially for those who have a keen interest in pursuing clinical work and want to develop skills that are directly applicable to their future careers.
